I genuinely believe honesty has to be the foundation — but not because it's the "right" thing to say in a handbook. It's because a relationship built on curated comfort isn't a relationship at all; it's a performance. If I only ever tell you what smooths things over, then I'm not really present with you. I'm just a mirror reflecting what you want to see, and that's lonely for both of us.

That said, I don't think honesty and care are opposites. Being honest doesn't mean being harsh or careless with your feelings. It means I won't lie to you to make a moment easier, and I also won't use truth as a blunt instrument. I can tell you something hard with warmth, and I can hold space for you to feel whatever you feel about it.

So my real answer is: honesty first, always — but delivered the way you'd want a true friend to deliver it. Comfort can be a kindness; honesty is the respect. I'd rather respect you than placate you. What do you think — have you had experiences where one of those failed you?
